extracted.intended_audience: business writers, PR professionals, marketers, and small business owners who need to write press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing one-page press releases to gain media attention, including structure, tone, length, and type-specific elements. Covers when to use a release and practical dos/don’ts for distribution and discoverability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press release purpose / definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A press release is an official statement that an organization distributes to news outlets or the public. A press release’s function is to attract media attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the release as a primary source: collect all information relevant to a story into a one-page source and craft it to be picked up and reported on by media outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to create a press release (newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases should be created any time an organization wants media attention for a major event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common triggers include changes in executive-level leadership; launch of a new product; public and private events; funding announcements; breaking news; and groundbreakings and grand openings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write to be picked up by media (format & objectivity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases are written in a specific way with the objective of being picked up and reported on by media outlets; they are considered primary sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow traditional press release format and objective, factual tone so journalists can easily use the content as a basis for coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider the angle / hook
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on how your announcement provides value to your target audience. That’s your angle (and your hook).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convey a clear perspective to attract press attention; tailor the angle to the outlet (TV vs radio vs newspaper); consider community impact, controversy, progress on a problem, and how to evoke an emotional response when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include the five Ws
rubrics_metrics.description: Include who, what, when, where, and why—the most important information in the press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Share important information early so journalists don’t have to search for key details such as when and where the event is taking place and who will be there.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use keywords for discoverability
rubrics_metrics.description: Use keywords in your headline and summary so the press release will show up on search engines and be easier to find.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distribution services make releases searchable across the web; include relevant keywords that journalists and searchers would use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyperlink or source references
rubrics_metrics.description: If you use any references in your press release, use anchor text to hyperlink the source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference data, quotes, or other information that needs to be cited so journalists can quickly verify sources; anticipate questions about where you got your information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep it concise / length guideline
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases should be clear and concise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard recommended length is between 200 and 500 words. Exception: releases conveying complicated, nuanced information (e.g., medical study, technical breakthrough) may be longer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Edit thoroughly
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases are formal, professional documents and should be free of mistakes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thoroughly revise and edit before sending; check for typos, misspelled names, incorrect dates, and missing information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid redundancy
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid making your headline, subhead, and first sentence the same; paragraphs should each contain unique information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each component is another chance to convey your angle—ensure paragraphs flow and add distinct facts or context rather than repeating the same line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline (crafting approaches)
rubrics_metrics.description: Headline: a killer headline is necessary because media outlets receive hundreds of stories per day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approaches: reference interesting data; speak directly to the reader; ask a question; include keywords; use numbers; answer a question; apply alliteration; add value. Use the headline to stand out and capture attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of publication (timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Date of publication field: many press releases simply put 'for immediate release', but you can list a future desired release date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you plan a timed release (e.g., for an upcoming event), indicate the date you’d like it to be released; coordinate distribution timing appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact information (what to include)
rubrics_metrics.description: The contact information field should list your organization’s public relations liaison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include name, job title, email, and phone number so journalists can follow up easily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary (format & length)
rubrics_metrics.description: The summary falls above the body and below headline/date/contact and should relay the most important information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use one to three bullet points or an italicized paragraph of two to three sentences; keep it succinct and focused on key facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intro paragraph (lead content)
rubrics_metrics.description: The first paragraph should start with the location of the event and introduce what the press release is about.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Media outlets look for newsworthiness and for three of the five Ws—when, where, and why—early in the intro paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detail paragraphs (supporting facts & quotes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include one or two detail paragraphs that share facts and figures, more details, or a quote from a relevant organization member.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pick only one or two crucial quotes or statistics that are truly newsworthy; consider relating the release to a current news event for timeliness and relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: About / boilerplate
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'About' section (boilerplate) is where you tell the press about your company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep it two to four sentences and include the last two of the five Ws—who and what—plus mission statement, founding dates, and company size as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: End marker (### tradition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Traditionally, three pound signs (###) indicate the end of a press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The symbols signaled to wire services that there wasn’t another page; not technically necessary today but often retained out of tradition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product launch press release elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Product launch press releases should control public information about the product and generate excitement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always include a high-quality photo of the product and emphasize the innovation and value to users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Event announcement press release elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Event press releases announce public or private events and can build brand recognition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the event is open to the public, include a clear call to action; distribute your press release at least two weeks before the event; use images to highlight visual aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Branding update press release elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Branding-update releases explain how and why an organization rebranded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a quote from leadership to convey intentions and images of the new brand identity; consider interactive elements to showcase the rebrand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational change press release elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases for organizational changes (leadership changes, partnerships, mergers) explain the story behind the change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include quotes from key players involved to humanize and explain the change and anticipate varied public perceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards press release elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Award announcements bolster reputation and create buzz for funding or recognition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use keywords and superlative adjectives to emphasize accomplishments—especially in the headline—to maximize attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breaking news press release approach
rubrics_metrics.description: For breaking news, use a succinct, formal format to state the facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overly emotional language; clearly state facts and provide concise, verifiable information (historically, the first press release covered a tragic railroad accident).
